assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Volt
items.clue: Unit meaning 1 J transferred for each coulomb passing between two places.

items.label: de Broglie wavelength
items.clue: The quantity h/p for any moving object; it gets shorter as momentum rises.

items.label: Electron gun
items.clue: Hot filament plus an accelerating potential of a few kV, producing the beam.

items.label: Electrical energy
items.clue: What charge hands over to a lamp as it passes through, though the charge itself comes out.

questions.stem: A steady current of 0.50 A flows through a small electric motor for 2.0 minutes. In this time, 360 J of energy is transferred from electrical energy to other forms in the motor. What is the potential difference across the motor?

An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?
While a kettle is heating water, 2.0 × 10³ C of charge passes through its heating element and 4.6 × 10⁵ J of energy is transferred in the element. What is the potential difference across the element?
A beam of electrons and a beam of protons are each accelerated from rest through 100 V and aimed at the same crystal, whose rows of atoms are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Which beam shows clear diffraction?

options.text: Only the protons: they are heavier, so they hit the atoms harder and are scattered more.
Both equally: they have the same charge and the same p.d., so they gain the same energy.
Only the electrons: their wavelength is comparable with the spacing of the atoms.
Neither: diffraction is a property of waves, and both beams are made of particles.
